description:
Found by defk-52v.3 (examples/lz4_snappy_decode.exs). An LZ4/Snappy decoder is copies: literals from the input and matches from earlier output. In the kernel subset the only way to write is out[i] = v per byte, so the copy helpers load 8 bytes with u64_le and store them with 8 byte writes; each store keeps a bounds check and an overflow check on o + i (disassembly: adds/b.vs, cmp/b.hs, strb per byte; clang does not merge the stores). liblz4 and snappy copy 8-16 bytes per instruction pair (wildcopy). Measured under load: the kernels are 2-7x slower than -O2/-O3 builds of the reference libraries and than lz4_flex; per element the kernel spends ~13 ns where liblz4 spends ~2 ns.

Options (pick one or both):
(a) word stores mirroring defk-n4r.2: out = put_u64_le(out, i, w) (and 32/16, _be), one check for i..i+7, Elixir mode as binary_part + <<w::little-64>> splice.
(b) a bounded copy builtin with the LZ meaning: out = copy(out, at, src, from, n) for distinct arrays (memcpy, one check of both ranges), and out = copy_back(out, at, off, n) with the forward byte-by-byte meaning when off < n (memmove is NOT that meaning; do 8-byte steps when off >= 8, a pattern fill when off < 8). Elixir mode: binary_part/:binary.copy as the example's Elixir decoder does.

Done when: lz4_snappy_decode.exs uses the new form, its copy loops have no per-byte checks in the fast-path report, the result agrees with Elixir mode on the corpus and fuzz, and the speed against the optimised NIF builds is re-measured.

comments.text:
Done (branch defk-52v.16/word-stores-copy, commit 7132bd9 + merge of main; not merged into main).

Design: option (b), the copy builtins; (a) word stores not added. The decoder's per-byte cost was the copies, and (b) removes the copy loops entirely (one check per copy); a word store would still be a check per word and leaves the loop. put_u64_le can come later if an encoder needs it.

- out = copy(out, at, src, from, n): out[at..at+n-1] = src[from..from+n-1], src as it was before the call (memmove, so src may be out). Elixir mode: binary_part splice.
- out = copy_back(out, at, off, n): out[at+j] = out[at+j-off] for j = 0..n-1 in order (LZ match; repeats when off < n, not memmove). Elixir mode: :binary.copy of the off-element pattern + binary_part.
- Any element type (same for out and src), positions/lengths in elements. Checks, same order and messages in both modes: n < 0 ArgumentError; destination range Enum.OutOfBoundsError (index = at); copy: source range (index = from); copy_back when n > 0: off < 1 ArgumentError, at - off < 0 OutOfBoundsError (index at - off). n == 0 skips the offset check (an LZ4 sequence with no match).
- Value semantics as a kernel that writes and returns its array parameter (same live set as inline/4): in place when nothing reads the old out after the call, else copied first (noted in the report). Tested: snapshot (b = a read later -> copied), branch (other arm reads -> in place), branch_after (read after the if -> copied), loop accumulator (no copy).
- Native (priv/defk_runtime.h defk_rcopy_T / defk_rcopy_back_T): <= 32 bytes loads-then-stores, else memmove; copy_back with off < n: 8-byte words from m >= 8 back (m = off, or the multiple of off >= 8 after < 8 single bytes: the pattern fill).
- Yielding: a copy of up to 1 MiB (DEFK_COPY_STRIP) runs at once and is charged DEFK_ZERO_TICKS(bytes) to the budget; a longer one returns -1 and the compiler's strip loop copies 1 MiB per step with a safepoint after each (like alloc zeroing; spills the args and bytes done; memmove strips run backwards when the destination overlaps the source from above; copy_back strips copy from the largest multiple of off back). yield: false or a length known <= 1 MiB: at once only. Tested with forced yields on 3 MiB copies (both directions, overlapping, offsets 1 and > strip), mutation-checked.

Example: lz4_snappy_decode.exs uses copy/copy_back in the arms of the reduce_while fn; copy_lit/copy_back helper kernels deleted; the defk-33b-era unconditional calls dropped (with the builtins they cost more: snappy 64 us unconditional vs 39-40 us branching; lz4 the same). Report: one note per copy ("one range check for the whole copy"); disassembly of the lz4 kernel: strb 36 -> 0, b.vs 74 -> 19 (snappy 36 -> 2 strb, both in the copy_back pattern fill; b.vs 72 -> 15). Corpus (20 blocks x 4 encoders) byte-identical; Elixir mode = native on 4 KB; fuzz 3000+3000 under forced yields (685 / 5230 yields) all agree, every rejection the kernels' own ArgumentError.

Numbers (provisional, load 140-195, Apple M4 Pro, best of 15-25 interleaved rounds, 3 runs; old kernels beside new in the same rounds), 64 KB JSON / 4 MB:
- snappy: old 64-65 us / 4.54 ms -> 38.6-39.8 us / 3.17 ms (example run 40-46 us); snappyer -O2 27-29 us / 1.6 ms -> 0.5-0.7x; Elixir optimised 175-235 us (4.6-5.5x).
- lz4: old 74-75 us / 4.24 ms -> 42.2-43.8 us / 2.69 ms (example 42-49 us); liblz4 -O3 9.1-9.6 us / 0.91 ms -> 0.2-0.35x; nimble_lz4 35-57 us / 1.23-1.33 ms; Elixir 240-420 us (4.8-6.6x).
- as-installed (-O0) NIFs: defk 1.2-2x faster. Repetitive 4 MB lz4: 175-180 us vs liblz4 -O3 190 us. Incompressible 4 MB: 85-93 us (was 0.95 ms), level with Elixir's sub-binary.
Remaining gap is per element (~8 ns per LZ4 sequence, from 13; liblz4 2 ns).

Docs: language.md Builtins rows + new "Range copies" section (runnable example), cheatsheet, compile-errors.md regenerated (builtin list), Defk.Report moduledoc, examples/README row, performance.md 2.15/7.6 updated, 6.15 marked superseded for copies, new 6.23. Tests: test/range_copy_test.exs (10 tests + 13 agreement properties, deep 10k runs passed).

Flagged: (1) n == 0 skips copy_back's offset check (conservative alternative was to always check; chosen so a no-match LZ element needs no branch). (2) A user kernel named like a builtin with matching types is silently replaced by it (the example's old copy_back/4 helper was): filed defk-pud. (3) A loop body holding a copy now has a safepoint per iteration (the cold strip loop counts as nested), as a helper with a loop did.

CI: format, compile --warnings-as-errors, credo --strict, dialyzer, ex_dna, reach, docs pass; mix test 1442/1444 with the known frames_live flakes (RaiseCleanupTest, BitstringHelperTest, defk-cwl comment), which pass/flake alone under load 196-213.

title: Word stores and a bounded array copy builtin, so a byte decoder does not pay a bounds and overflow check per byte
